kinds.cover_source: NFPA 24 10.4.1: an underground fire service main buried below the frost line, with 2.5 ft cover the least where frost is no factor; 36 in is the usual specification
IFGC 404.12: underground gas piping with 12 in cover the least (18 in in yards and under drives, the usual specification)
trade practice: a building sewer leaves the building with about 2 ft over its crown where neither the plans nor the plumbing sheets print its invert
IPC 305.4.1 and trade practice: a water service buried below the frost line; 36 in cover the usual specification where the plans print no depth

sheet_source: a civil sheet whose title names utility work (UTILITY LAYOUT, WATER AND SEWER PLAN) is the plan the services into the building are drawn on, whatever the classifier makes of a title with no PLAN in it; its details and profiles are not plans
fit_source: a civil plan at its printed scale whose building outline is no closed line (drawn in pieces, its layers flattened): the building's walls matched to the plan's linework, searched around the plan's BUILDING labels at each quarter turn of the plan's lines (refined within 1.5 deg), the turn and place where most of the walls lie on lines running along them (60% at least, and 10 points over any other place or turn)
line_source: a civil utility plan's service: the line its label (size and service, as printed) lies along or its leader points at, followed through the meter, backflow or valve vault drawn between its pieces (same layer, 25 ft at most across a symbol) to the building it ends at (15 ft at most from the building outline the plan draws)
poc_source: trade practice and the usual Division 22 and 33 split: the building's trades own each service from 5 ft outside the wall (the civil plan's note at the line governs; a building drain's code limit is 30 in, IPC 202)
join_source: the service joined to the building's own entry of its system the plumbing or fire protection plans draw nearest where it reaches the wall (under the slab, at the service's depth)
undesignated_source: a private water line the civil plan names neither domestic nor fire: the fire service where the building takes a separate domestic line or only a fire protection entry is by it, else the domestic water service (verify with the plumbing and fire protection plans)
slope_source: IPC Table 704.1: drainage piping 2-1/2 in and less 1/4 in per ft, 3 to 6 in 1/8 in per ft, 8 in and larger 1/16 in per ft
grade_source: trade practice: finished grade at the building about 6 in below the finished floor (IBC 1804.4 slopes it away)
scope_source: the documents' point of connection: the building's trade from it to the building, the site/civil contractor from it to the main
